title: The Mindvalley Training System
overview: Vishen explains the thinking behind how Mindvalley turns experts into recognised authorities, and introduces the four-month Expert to Authority Mastery built on that method. You hear why he believes authority is a learnable method rather than a gift, what the 3,000-person summit survey revealed about where expert businesses break down, and how the five-pillar curriculum, weekly implementation labs and AI skill packs are designed to close that gap.
key_ideas: The authority gap is the distance between what you know and how the market perceives you. Vishen's position is that the gap can be engineered closed: the people getting the client, the stage and the press are rarely more qualified, they have simply learned the systems.

The market cannot hire an expert it cannot find. Being findable (social media, SEO, organic traffic, influencer marketing, advertising) is a separate problem from being good, and both have to be solved.

Authority is a method, not a gift. People are born with articulation, a genius brain or a passion, but the method for scaling an audience has to be learned, and the same machine has worked across very different niches (Lifebook, Regan Hillyer, Marisa Peer, Jim Kwik).

When 3,000 summit registrants were asked where their business was breaking down, the two most common answers were 'nobody knows I exist' and 'I can't put what I do into words'. Vishen treats these as the day-one problems to solve, then builds systems so you never get stuck expressing yourself again.

Learning only sticks when it is applied the same week. The programme pairs every teaching session with an implementation lab so that a new component of the business is birthed each week rather than sitting as notes on paper.

AI tools should be built to learn and self-evolve. Vishen's 'skill packs' are meant to get better with every email and page you produce, and the same principle applies to your team: his company went from 400 people to around 200 with heavy AI use and higher output.

Partnership and collaboration are relationship work, not transactions. Vishen describes the teachers he works with as friends rather than clients, and credits that way of structuring partnerships with why they show up for each other.

Legacy means a business that outlives you and survives your absence, so that a two-week camping trip you promised your child does not stop revenue. This is the final pillar because everything else is built towards it.

A flagship course anchors everything else. Vishen's own flagship is the Silva programme and it drives the rest of his product ladder; the Dawn Huang story (from $300 an hour to $800 an hour with a 2,000-person waiting list in one year) illustrates what happens when a talented practitioner applies the method rather than staying at the same rate for a decade.

frameworks.name: The four authority-gap questions
steps: Have you ever watched someone less qualified than you get the client, the stage or the press, and asked why it wasn't you?
Do you privately know your work is better than your results suggest?
If more people simply knew you existed, would your income change?
Do you already know roughly what has been stopping you?

frameworks.name: Five pillars of the Expert to Authority curriculum
steps: Messaging and positioning: niche, vision, standing out, signature method, high-value signature offers, persuasion, copywriting and influence
Platform and content: designing your course, building a publishing machine, AI skill packs, scaling social media, the Oversubscribed funnel process
Funnel and conversion: paid advertising, funnel design, webinar and VSL playbooks, email marketing
Scale and products: membership, high-ticket one-to-one coaching, owning the stage, building a digital brain, building teams of humans with AI companions, partnerships and collaboration
Legacy and systems: building a business that outlives you

frameworks.name: Weekly learn-and-build rhythm
steps: Tuesday: live content session that goes deep on one principle (for example email), with structure, templates and AI skills
Friday: live implementation lab with other students and a trained AI facilitator, applying the principle to your own business
Every session is live and recorded; budget about three hours a week of attendance

frameworks.name: Ten outcomes the programme is designed around
steps: Own a category instead of competing in one

Expertise turned into an offer people pay a premium for
A course that sells itself through results
Never running out of things to say
A funnel that runs while you sleep
An email list that becomes your most valuable asset
Revenue that renews itself
High-ticket offers
A business that does not need you in the room

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: What does it actually take to move these concepts from notes on paper into your business, so you see the same results Vishen, Jimmy and John have been showing?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Over 22 years I've built brands for about 100 teachers. The next evolution is to teach that method to the next group of aspiring teachers and leaders, and how deep you go depends on where you are: for some the summit is enough, and for those who want to scale to their first 10 million there is a four-month curriculum.

programme_summary: Vishen announced Expert to Authority Mastery, a four-month live programme running October 2026 to January 2027: 18 weeks, 36 live sessions, with a live teaching call and an implementation lab each week, all recorded. Vishen is the main teacher, with guest teachers Daniel Priestley, Jimmy Naraine, John Lee and Ajit Nawalkha, and the cohort is planned at around 500 people including a number of Mindvalley teachers. The curriculum follows five pillars (messaging and positioning, platform and content, funnel and conversion, scale and products, legacy and systems) and includes the community platform, summit and Mastery recordings, a certificate of completion, and an opening 'Authority Skill Pack' session with Vishen on Friday 25 September where the AI skills shown at the summit are installed. Vishen stated the price on stage as $4,999 (or four payments of $1,499), with a $500 discount for Mindvalley members and a full refund available at any time in the first two weeks. Those enrolling by Monday 21 September were also offered a Mindvalley Accelerator workshop with Jimmy Naraine (four to six hours) to build their flagship course.
next_steps: Write your honest answers to the four authority-gap questions and name the one thing you already suspect has been holding you back.
Decide which of the two survey breakdowns is yours (nobody knows I exist, or I can't put what I do into words) and draft a one-sentence statement of what you do.
Identify your flagship course or offer: the one product that everything else in your ladder should drive towards.
Review the programme overview and, if you are considering enrolling, make sure you have an AI subscription and can attend Tuesdays and Fridays at the stated times.
attribution_notes: The transcript labels Vishen's lines 'Vishen' and the host's lines 'Mindvalley'; Jason Goldberg introduces and closes the session and all other content is Vishen speaking to slides. Attribution is high confidence throughout. Names were corrected from the transcription (Vishin Lakiani, Marissa Pierre, Reagan Hillier, Jimmy Naren, Ajit Nawalka, Daniel Prisley); the kickoff date is given in this transcript as '20th of September' but Vishen also says the programme starts 'Friday, six days from now', which is 25 September, and Day 3 confirms 25 September, so that date is used.
